title: Hal Sets Up a Pen
lines: Hal has ten hens but not a pen.
"The hens are in the mud," said Dad.
Hal gets logs. Dad cuts the logs.
Hal digs and sets a log in the pit.
Ten logs, and the pen is up!
The hens hop in. He pats his hens.
The hens are not in the mud.

questions.ask: What did Hal use to make the pen?
questions.listenFor: Logs - ten of them, cut by Dad. It is said in the story. Have your child point to the line that tells you, then read it out loud again.

questions.ask: How do you know the pen worked?
questions.listenFor: The hens are not in the mud at the end. Listen for the not-in-the-mud part, not just "it worked."

questions.ask: Do you think Hal could put up the pen on his own? Tell me why.
questions.listenFor: No wrong answer here. You want a reason pulled from the story - Dad did the cutting, or Hal did the digging and the setting up. A reason beats a yes or no.
